hypothesis: On a flat plate the chord between markers equals their geodesic distance and the Jacobi transfer is [[1, s], [0, 1]], so the plate isolates instrument, frame and procedure error from curvature.
input_data: Declared 300 x 300 x 6 mm plate, 5 x 5 marker grid at 60 mm pitch
Offset perturbations: 2 mm lateral, 5 mrad heading
mathematical_model: Plane z = 0; geodesics are straight lines; j'' = 0 gives j_lat = 1, j_head = s; offset-path separation e(s) = delta + s dtheta.
numerical_result: max |chord - geodesic| = 5.68e-14 mm; max |Phi(240) - exact| = 0; heading-offset separation at 240 mm = 1.2 mm.
observation_model: No observation. The protocol specifies camera/CMM observation of the markers, the tape start poses and the offset tapes; its hardware-evidence slot is empty.

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.

recommended_next_task: Acquire MFG-FLAT-PLATE-01 and bind its camera export to T138 (ciw lab run T138 --capture photogrammetry=<targets.csv>, format ciw.lab-mfg-target-capture.v1), then retain the run with ciw lab hardware retain; T138's pair comparison of the captured chords is computational, and a physical label needs a metrology instrument probe or a signed-capture trust anchor (deferred research question). title: Design a flat-plate control experiment.
uncertainty: Rounding only (flat metric, zero Christoffel symbols). Measurement uncertainty is declared, not known.
unresolved_assumptions: Real plate flatness (declared 0.05 mm) and thermal state are not measured; their effect is bounded only by the declared tolerance.
Instrument uncertainties are declared planning values, not calibrated values.
On the plane the chord-geodesic comparison is a zero-curvature sanity check of the shooting machinery: RK4 and the Jacobi heading field are exact there, so it cannot detect curvature errors.
